Lina: Quick PSA — saw a new OOM pattern on AWQ+FP8 runs when we hit mixed-seq workloads.
Jorge: Details? repro? :eyes:
Lina: Short summary: small queries (<=64) get upcast+copy churn from kernel fallback, leaves lots of small free fragments in slab allocator. Memory map shows many 4-16KB holes.
Priya: That rings a bell. Did perf-bot capture the timeline?
perf-bot: perf snapshot 1893456789: GRP=awq_fp8_mixed; peak_gpu=28.9GB; alloc_ops=12.4k; avg_alloc_size=48KB; fragmentation=19%.
Kai: Can you paste the allocator debug dump?
Lina: Sure — truncated: ```
slab_pool: total=32GB
active_chunks: 412K
free_chunks_by_size:
  4KB: 82K
  8KB: 60K
  16KB: 10K
largest_free_block: 256KB
frag_ratio: 0.21
```
Jorge: Oof. Continuous-batching makes small temp buffers for kernel upcast and they never coalesce because freelist is size-bucketed.
Priya: Proposed mitigation: introduce a "soft-merge" pass on idle windows that coalesces adjacent small free pages into 1MB pages, but gated behind a latency SLO check. Thoughts?
Kai: I like soft-merge. Concern: GC could spike latency if run mid-inference. We should coordinate with batching heuristics to prefer larger-kernel selection when sequence length distribution is skewed.
Lina: Agreed. Another quick win: when we detect fp8->fp32 fallback path, mark those temp buffers as "ephemeral" and allocate from a fast bump region that gets reclaimed wholesale. Avoids freelist churn.
Jorge: Ephemeral bump allocator + periodic compaction seems ideal. Any numbers?
perf-bot: quick sim (canary): ephemeral-bump + soft-merge -> peak_gpu=27.1GB (-1.8GB), fragmentation=8%, p99 latency change +0.9ms on small seq.
Priya: Nice. p99 < +1ms is acceptable for canary. We need a rollout plan: feature flag, canary on 5 nodes, perf-trace, and auto-disable if p99 regresses >2ms.
Lina: I'll draft an RFC and prototype. Action items: @Jorge - wire ephemeral bump + metric tags; @Kai - add soft-merge background task with safety window; @Priya - define canary gates and alert thresholds.
Jorge: On it. I'll also add allocator-level hints for quantization kernels to request aligned 1MB scratch spaces to reduce fragmentation.
Kai: Small note: avoid forcing alignment for small kernels that already fit in L2-friendly buffers, we should be adaptive.
Priya: I'll update the rollout doc and create the canary job.
Lina: Thanks — will attach profiler traces to the RFC. In-thread repro command if anyone wants to run locally: ```PYTHONPATH=./pybench python perf/run_gpu_repro.py --model gpt-6b-awq --seq-dist mixed --iters 200 --record-trace /tmp/trace.zip```
Jorge: Good. If we get the memory map down and frag <10% we should avoid the OOMs we've been chasing.
perf-bot: noted. created perf-ticket #INF-1819 with snapshot and canary metrics.
deploy-bot: canary cluster flag created: runtime.alloc.ephemeral=true, runtime.alloc.soft_merge=deferred
Lina: Great — will follow up in the RFC thread. :thumbsup:
